description: Sprint R intent catalog fixture. Family x entity coverage matrix for the smith fast-path classifier (docs/v5-smith-experience.md s2.7). Every answerable pair has a named live source; gaps are explicit. S2's coverage-matrix test instantiates families from live config at runtime and pins the EXPECTED coverage against this fixture so a newly tracked entity missing from the classifier fails a test instead of silently going unaskable. Entities mined from: checks.go registry (16 checks), propose.go (proposers + servicePortUnit), execute.go (restartAllowed allowlist), binaries.go + smith.binaries.tracked, the KB corpus (mesh inventory doc, corpus entries, pitfalls), the deployment DB (smith_findings, smith_actions, smith_investigations, notifications), and live seam probes (journalctl as the daemon operating user, tailscale version CLI, ComfyUI /system_stats). Reachability mesh entities follow a SYNTHETIC two-host example deployment (host 'alpha', peer 'beta') — two-layer knowledge architecture: real inventories are deployment data imported via smith.mesh.services, never fixtures.

kernel_params.verdict: STAYS runbook - needs bootloader edit + reboot (genuinely out of reach)

runbook_audit.summary: 3 runbook proposers exist (kernel_params, gtt_ceiling, binary_versions). ALL 3 are correctly runbook-only - each has a real reason it can't be an executable kind (reboot, guardrail 2, compile window). NO runbook->executable promotions needed.

The composite (check_id, created_at) the plan floated is unnecessary at this row count and these query shapes; even at 10k+ rows the check_id index alone makes these index scans.
